response.justification: The candidate is a highly experienced, versatile senior engineer with 15+ years of delivery across web, mobile, embedded and distributed systems, and demonstrable strength in performance-sensitive, event-driven architectures (low-latency microservices at Sociomantic handling millions of requests/second, an event-driven geo-data platform). However, the role's core requirement is hands-on senior C++ development, and the resume shows only ~7 months of professional C++ (National Instruments, 2014-2015) plus a university thesis project; C++ is not even listed in the skills section. There is also no evidence of the domain-critical requirements: IEC 62443 / Secure Development Lifecycle, MQTT, industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, IEC 61850), industrial automation, or Azure. The transferable skills are real, but the gap on the primary technical axis and the security/OT domain is too wide for a mid-senior specialist hire.
strengths: Deep experience with high-performance, low-latency, event-driven distributed systems
Strong engineering craft: TDD, CI/CD, testing tooling, mentoring, workshops and public talks
Broad polyglot background including systems languages (D, C, C++, Java) and full-stack delivery
concerns: Minimal professional C++/STL experience — roughly 7 months, over a decade ago
No exposure to IEC 62443, SDL practices, or industrial cybersecurity standards
No industrial automation, MQTT, OPC UA/Modbus, or Azure cloud background

key_factors.factor: Industrial automation & IEC 62443 security domain gap
